Units: Shore A; Shore D; Rockwell M; Rockwell R; Shore (scale not specified by source)

Description: How much a moulded or printed part shrinks as it cools, to ISO 294-4 or ASTM D955. A sheet that prints it parallel and normal to the flow publishes two rows.
Resistance through the body of the material, to IEC 60093 or ASTM D257. It is what separates a conductive or ESD grade from an insulating one.
Resistance across the surface, to IEC 60093 or ASTM D257.
The field a material holds before it breaks down, to IEC 60243 or ASTM D149.
The dielectric constant, to IEC 60250 or ASTM D150. A sheet states the frequency it was measured at, which the row keeps as its test condition.
The voltage at which a wetted, contaminated surface begins to track, to IEC 60112. A sheet may print it as a stage rather than a voltage; only a voltage is a value here.
The least oxygen concentration that sustains burning, to ISO 4589 or ASTM D2863. A flammability class (UL 94 V-0, HB) is a certification claim, not this.
The force per thickness that tears a specimen, to ISO 34 or ASTM D624. Published for elastomers and films.
The volume a standard abrasive removes, to ISO 4649 or DIN 53516. A smaller number wears less.
How much of a compression an elastomer keeps after the load is taken off, to ISO 815 or ASTM D395. A sheet states the time and temperature, which the row keeps as its test conditions.
How much a specimen narrows as it is stretched.
Where the material begins to break down rather than melt, by thermogravimetry (ISO 11358). A sheet states the mass loss it is quoted at, commonly 5 %, which the row keeps as its test condition.
